info.name: oracle API
info.description:
HTTP API of the oracle, started with `go run ./cmd/oracle api` (or the `api` command of the Docker image).

The server listens on the port in `PORT` (default `8080`) and connects to Postgres with the `DB_*` variables before it starts listening: if the database is unreachable, the process exits and nothing answers.

There is no authentication. Responses are JSON unless noted; routes that don't exist answer `404` and known routes called with the wrong method answer `405` with an `Allow` header, both in plain text.

Set `baseUrl` to the server you are calling. The default points at a local run.

variable.description: Address of the oracle API, without a trailing slash.

item.name: Infra
item.description: Service status. The Swagger UI at `/swagger/index.html` documents the same routes.

request.description:
Reports that the server is up, with the current server time in UTC (RFC 3339).

The database connection is checked once at startup, not on every call, so a `200` means the process is running and was able to connect when it started.

Only `GET` and `HEAD` are accepted; any other method answers `405 Method Not Allowed` with `Allow: GET, HEAD`. No side effects; safe to call repeatedly, for example from a load balancer or monitor.

item.name: Tickers
item.description: Tickers and their daily quotes, loaded from B3 by `oracle sync`. Read-only `GET` routes that answer JSON, errors included (`{"error": "..."}`).

request.description:
Every ticker with quotes in the database, of any spec (stocks, real estate funds, ETFs, BDRs), in ticker order.

`name`, `spec` and `isin` come from the latest quote of each ticker; `spec` has B3's padding collapsed (`PN N2`). `first_session` and `last_session` are `YYYY-MM-DD`; `sessions` counts the days with a quote.

An empty database answers `[]`. A database failure answers `500` with `{"error":"internal error"}`. Read only.

exec: pm.test("is a list of tickers", function () {

request.description:
Summary of one ticker, as in *List tickers*, plus `last_quote`: its quote on `last_session`.

The ticker is case-insensitive (`petr4` works). A ticker without quotes answers `404` with `{"error":"ticker ZZZZ3 not found"}`. Read only.

exec: pm.test("ticker with its latest quote", function () {

item.name: List the quotes of a ticker

request.description:
Daily quotes of one ticker, in date order. Prices are in BRL as traded, **not adjusted** for splits or dividends; `volume` is the traded value in BRL.

`from` and `to` are optional and inclusive; without them the whole history is returned. A range without sessions answers `[]`.

Errors: `400` when `from` or `to` is not `YYYY-MM-DD` or `from` is after `to`; `404` for a ticker without quotes. Read only.

item.name: Sessions
item.description: Trading days stored in the database. Read-only `GET` routes that answer JSON, errors included (`{"error": "..."}`).

request.description:
The last day with quotes in the database (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and `stale`: `true` when it is more than 4 days old, which means a sync is missing (the same rule `oracle recommend` warns about).

An empty database answers `404` with `{"error":"no quotes stored yet, run oracle sync"}`. Read only.

response.name: 404 Not Found
response.body: {"error":"no quotes stored yet, run oracle sync"}

item.name: List the quotes of a session

request.description:
Every quote of one trading day, of any spec, in ticker order. Same fields as *List the quotes of a ticker*.

Errors: `400` when the date is not `YYYY-MM-DD`; `404` when there is no session that day (weekend, holiday or not synced yet). Read only.

item.name: Strategy
item.description: The swing rule of `internal/swing`, the same functions `oracle recommend` and `oracle backtest` call. Read-only `GET` routes that answer JSON, errors included.

request.description:
The parameters of the swing rule used by `oracle recommend` and `oracle backtest`.

A signal is a close above the 200-day average with RSI(2) below `oversold`. After the signal close, the plan is a limit buy `entry_atr` ATRs below the close, a target `target_atr` ATRs above it and a stop `stop_atr` ATRs below it (ATR of 14 sessions), selling at the close after `max_hold` sessions otherwise. `cost_pct` is charged per side, in percent. A stock is eligible with at least `min_trades` trades and positive expectancy, and is analyzed only with a median volume of `min_volume` BRL. `warmup` is the number of sessions before the first signal.

The `oversold` shown is the strongest tier; see *List the signal tiers*. Read only.

The signal levels, strongest first. `oracle recommend` stops at the first tier, or goes down the list with `-fill` until it has enough stocks.

`oversold` is the RSI(2) the close must be below; `101` (`tendência`) means no pullback is required. Labels and rules are in Portuguese, as the CLI prints them. Read only.

exec: pm.test("tiers from strongest to weakest", function () {

query.description: Signal tier: forte (default), médio, fraco or tendência; accents are optional (medio, tendencia).
Years of history, 1 to 30 (default 3, as oracle recommend).

variable.description: B3 ticker of a stock (ON, PN or UNT), case-insensitive.

request.description:
Runs the rule on the last `years` of one stock: whether its latest close (`as_of`) is a signal for the `tier`, the order prices for the next session (`levels`, `null` without a signal) and its track record. `win_rate`, `avg_return` and `expectancy` are fractions (`0.01` = 1%), net of costs; `expectancy` shrinks the average toward 0 for short records and is what `oracle recommend` ranks by.

Runs `internal/swing`, the same functions `oracle recommend` calls, so the numbers match the CLI. Only the part of the series after the last split counts (prices are not adjusted); with fewer than 260 sessions there, or a median volume below `min_volume`, the track record is empty and there is no signal.

Errors: `400` for an unknown `tier` or `years` outside 1–30; `404` for a ticker without quotes in the period; `422` when the ticker is not a stock (real estate funds, ETFs and BDRs are not analyzed). Read only.

item.name: List the simulated trades of a stock

query.description: Signal tier: forte (default), médio, fraco or tendência; accents are optional (medio, tendencia).
Years of history, 1 to 30 (default 3, as oracle recommend).

variable.description: B3 ticker of a stock (ON, PN or UNT), case-insensitive.

request.description:
The trades behind the track record of *Analyze a stock*, in date order: each signal (`signal_date`) is bought with the limit order the next session (`entry_date`) and sold at the target, the stop or the close of the last holding session (`exit_date`). `entry` and `exit` are BRL; `return` is a fraction net of costs. Signals while a trade is open are skipped.

Runs `internal/swing`, the same functions `oracle recommend` calls, so the numbers match the CLI. Only the part of the series after the last split counts (prices are not adjusted); with fewer than 260 sessions there, or a median volume below `min_volume`, the track record is empty and there is no signal. In that case the list is `[]`.

Errors: `400` for an unknown `tier` or `years` outside 1–30; `404` for a ticker without quotes in the period; `422` when the ticker is not a stock (real estate funds, ETFs and BDRs are not analyzed). Read only.

request.description:
Every stock traded on the latest session (`session`) whose close fires the rule of the `tier`, each with the fields of *Analyze a stock*: the candidates `oracle recommend` picks from, before analyst targets and position sizing. Eligible stocks come first, then by expectancy. `[]` in `signals` means no signal in that tier.

Loads the history of every stock for `years`, so it is the slowest route. Errors: `400` for an unknown `tier` or `years` outside 1–30; `404` when no stock quotes are stored in the period. Read only.
